experiment: Horizon toolchain BPU performance estimate for the v3 candidate

claim_scope.note: produced by the OpenExplorer toolchain on the workstation; NOT a board measurement, no power, no real DDR/BPU counters

toolchain.compile_options: opt=2, jobs=16, balance=100, debug=true (single BPU core)

basis.identity_cross_check: the toolchain's int8 MACs (249,320,448) and Conv ops (498,640,896) are exactly the
values challenge/flops_report.json reports and B3 independently recomputed, so the
estimate is bound to the measured model, not to a stale artifact
basis.bottleneck: summed layer load time 616 us vs summed compute time 121 us over 47 layers -> the
estimate is DDR/load bound, not MAC bound

interval_compute_utilization.reading: average computing-unit utilization inside one inference is ~14%; the model is memory bound

caveats: toolchain estimate, not J6P board latency; no BPU/DDR counters were read
single BPU core configuration; a multi-core deployment would change latency and utilization
the DDR bandwidth figure is the tool's memory model, not a measured bus trace
CONV/LINEAR op counts exclude attention, normalization, activation and data movement
the utilization number above is the compute-unit utilization inside one inference; the official heterogeneous-utilization formula (end-to-end CPU/GPU/NPU/DSP) is still B2/A4's
how_to_reproduce: in the official image: hb_compile with the A2 calibration yaml, then read student_v0_v3.json (or the html report) for performance/DDR/interval sections
